skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count to 20 by 1s
skills.description: What number comes next when you count by 1s? Start at any number, like 7, 8, 9, and keep going to 20.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: What numbers are used for
skills.description: Numbers tell us how many, which one is first or second, and names like player number 24. Pick how the number is being used.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: See up to 5 at once
skills.description: Look quickly at some dots and tell how many there are, without counting one by one.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and type numbers to 20
skills.description: Match numbers from 0 to 20 to groups of things. Tap or type the number you see.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Counting up and counting down
skills.description: Count up and the number gets bigger. Count down and it gets smaller. Which way did it go?

skills.subject: math
skills.title: More, less, or the same
skills.description: Look at two groups and tell which has more, which has less, or if they are the same.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare numbers from 0 to 20
skills.description: Tell which of two numbers is greater or less. Find the number that is 1 or 2 more, or 1 or 2 less.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Estimate, then count to check
skills.description: Guess how many things there are. Is it closer to 5 or to 10? Then count to check.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Break apart and build 10
skills.description: Show that a number is made of two smaller parts, like 6 is 4 and 2. Find the missing part.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and take away to 5
skills.description: Put groups together or take some away when the numbers stay 5 or less. Know answers like 2 and 3 make 5.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 10
skills.description: Solve story problems about joining, taking away, parts, and comparing, with answers up to 10. Use counters or fingers to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Share equally
skills.description: Share things so every friend gets the same amount. Tell how many each friend gets.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Coins and bills
skills.description: Name Canadian coins and bills and tell what each is worth, up to 10 dollars. Loonies and toonies are coins too!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and show numbers to 50
skills.description: Read numbers up to 50 in words and digits, and match them to tens and ones. Pick how a number is used, like on a clock or a house.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Skip count to 50
skills.description: Count to 50 by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s. What number comes next when you count by 5s? Use a number line or hundred chart to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 50
skills.description: Tell which number is greater or less. Put numbers up to 50 in order from least to greatest, or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Estimate up to 50, then count
skills.description: Guess how many things are in a group. Is it closer to 20 or to 50? Then count to check.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Build and break apart numbers
skills.description: Put numbers together or break them into parts, like 28 is 20 and 8, or 10 and 10 and 8. The amount stays the same.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fair shares for 2 or 4
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap what each friend gets when 2 or 4 friends share. Leftovers can be cut into equal pieces.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Halves and fourths
skills.description: Learn that one half of a whole is the same as two fourths of that same whole. Two halves or four fourths make one whole.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare shares of a whole
skills.description: When a whole is shared with more friends, each piece gets smaller. Look at the pictures and tap the biggest or smallest piece.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract facts to 10
skills.description: Know addition facts up to 10 and the take-away facts that go with them. For example, 4 and 6 make 10, so 10 take away 4 is 6.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Any order, zero, and checking
skills.description: Adding in any order gives the same answer, and adding or taking away zero changes nothing. Use adding to check a take-away answer.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting to 20
skills.description: Use tricks like counting on, making 10, and near doubles to add and subtract in your head. Your answers stay 20 or less.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 50
skills.description: Use pictures, number lines, and equations to solve stories about joining, taking away, and comparing, up to 50. Find the missing number too.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal groups up to 10
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap how many in all, like 5 groups of 2, or 6 groups of one half. Or find how many groups there are.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 200
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 200 with hundreds, tens, and ones. Break numbers apart in different ways, like 124 is 100 and 24, or 12 tens and 4 ones.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 200
skills.description: Tell which number is greater or less, up to 200. Put numbers in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Skip count to 200
skills.description: What number comes next when you count by 20s, 25s, or 50s? Start at any number and count up to 200, with coins or a number line to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Estimate up to 200, then count
skills.description: Guess how many are in a big group. Is it closer to 50, 100, or 200? Count a small bunch first to help, then count to check.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Even and odd numbers
skills.description: An even number can be split into pairs with none left over. An odd number always has one left over.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fair shares with leftover pieces
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap what each friend gets when up to 10 things are shared by 2, 3, 4, or 6 friends. Leftovers get cut into pieces, like 3 and one third.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: One third equals two sixths
skills.description: Share the same whole in thirds or in sixths. See that one third is the same amount as two sixths.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Adding and subtracting rules and checks
skills.description: Adding in any order gives the same answer, and zero changes nothing. Use adding to check taking away, and use equal jumps to see how adding links to multiplying.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract facts to 20
skills.description: Know adding facts with totals up to 20, like 9 + 9 = 18, and the take-away facts that go with them. Use doubles and making 10 to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting to 50
skills.description: Add and subtract in your head with answers up to 50. Try counting on, making 10s, or taking away in parts.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 100
skills.description: Use objects, pictures, and equations to solve stories about joining, taking away, and comparing, up to 100. Find the missing number, wherever it hides.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal groups and repeated adding
skills.description: Find how many in all when there are equal groups, like 4 groups of 5. Groups of one half and one fourth count too.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Share up to 12 equally
skills.description: Share up to 12 things equally. Find how many in each group, or how many groups you can make.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 1000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 1000 with hundreds, tens, and ones. Match them to words, digits, and spots on a number line, like 638 is 600 + 30 + 8.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Place value of each digit
skills.description: Tell what each digit is worth in a number, like the 5 in 511 means 5 hundreds. See that a zero holds a place and that each place is ten times bigger than the one next to it.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 1000
skills.description: Tell which of two numbers is greater or less, up to 1000. Put numbers in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round to 10 or 100
skills.description: Find the closest ten or hundred to a number, like 237 is about 240 or about 200. Use rounding to make a quick guess.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Skip count to 1000
skills.description: Count up to 1000 by 1s, 50s, 100s, and 200s. Start at any number and keep going, using a number line to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fair shares of up to 20
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap what each friend gets when up to 20 things are shared by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, or 10 friends. It can be a whole and a part, like 2 and two thirds.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Same share, different fractions
skills.description: See that different fractions can name the same amount, like one half and two fourths, or one fifth and two tenths. Use fair-share pictures to show it.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Show times and divide with arrays
skills.description: Use rows and columns of dots, called arrays, to show multiplying up to 10 × 10 and dividing up to 100 ÷ 10. Tell how many rows, how many in each row, and how many in all.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Facts for 2, 5, and 10
skills.description: Know the times facts for 2, 5, and 10, like 6 × 5 = 30. Know the matching share facts too, like 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide rules
skills.description: Use rules to help you multiply, like 4 × 5 is the same as 5 × 4, and 4 × 6 is 4 × 5 plus 4 × 1. Use multiplying to check a divide answer.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide stories
skills.description: Solve stories about equal groups using hops on a number line or pictures. Some groups can be one half, one fourth, or one third, and you can find the total, the groups, or the size of each group.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions as adding unit pieces
skills.description: See that three fifths is one fifth added three times. In a fraction like 3/5, the bottom number tells the size of the pieces and the top number counts them.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Scaling by 2, 5, and 10
skills.description: Use the pairs 1 to 2, 1 to 5, and 1 to 10 to make numbers bigger. If 1 smiley is 5 kids, then 3 smileys are 15 kids.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting to 1000
skills.description: Add and subtract in your head with totals up to 1000, using tricks like making 10, adding in parts, or adjusting. Round first to make a quick guess.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Column adding and subtracting
skills.description: Add and subtract bigger numbers by lining up hundreds, tens, and ones. Trade ten ones for a ten, or a ten for ones, when you need to.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 1000
skills.description: Solve stories about joining, taking away, and comparing, with numbers up to 1000. Use number lines, pictures, or column adding, and find the missing number wherever it hides.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 10 000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 10 000 with thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones. Break them apart in different ways, like 8621 is 8000 + 600 + 20 + 1.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 10 000
skills.description: Tell which of two numbers is greater or less, up to 10 000. Put numbers in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round to 10, 100, or 1000
skills.description: Find the closest ten, hundred, or thousand to a number, like 1237 is about 1200. If it is exactly in the middle, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions from halves to tenths
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap the fraction it shows, like 3/4 or 7/10. Know what the bottom number and the top number mean.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order fair shares
skills.description: Look at the pictures and tap who gets more when a whole is shared by different numbers of friends. Put the shares in order from least to greatest.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count and add unit fractions
skills.description: Count by halves, thirds, fourths, and more, even past one whole, like 5 thirds. See that 4 one-thirds added up is 4 × 1/3, or 4/3.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and compare decimal tenths
skills.description: Read, show, compare, and order numbers like 0.6 and 24.7. The first digit after the dot counts tenths.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round decimals to whole numbers
skills.description: Round a number like 1.7 to the closest whole number. If it is exactly halfway, like 2.5, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions and decimal tenths match
skills.description: Show that fractions and decimals can name the same amount, like 1/2 and 0.5, or 15 tenths and 1.5.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Rules and checks for operations
skills.description: Use rules like order, grouping, and splitting numbers to help you solve problems. Use opposite operations to check your answers.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide facts to 100
skills.description: Know all the times facts up to 10 × 10 and the divide facts that go with them, like 7 × 6 = 42 and 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Use facts you know to find new ones.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply by 10, 100, and 1000
skills.description: In your head, multiply a number by 10, 100, or 1000, or divide it by 10. Each digit moves to a new place.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting with tenths
skills.description: Add and subtract decimals like 14.9 + 24.6 in your head. Try making a friendly number, then fix it after.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract to 10 000
skills.description: Solve stories and problems by adding and subtracting numbers up to 10 000 and decimal tenths. Use number lines, pictures, or column adding.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply by a one-digit number
skills.description: Multiply two- or three-digit numbers by a one-digit number, or by 10, 100, or 1000. Use arrays and split the number into parts to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide bigger numbers, share leftovers
skills.description: Divide two- or three-digit numbers by a one-digit number. When there is something left over, share it too, like 33 ÷ 4 = 8 and 1/4.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Rates: amounts per group
skills.description: Show rates like 2 trapezoids per hexagon or 5 stickers per strip. Use pictures and tools to find how many in all.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 100 000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 100 000 in words, digits, and expanded form. Break them apart by place value, like 24 336 is 2 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 3 hundreds, 3 tens, and 6 ones.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 100 000
skills.description: Tell which of two big numbers is greater or less by checking the biggest place that is different. Put numbers up to 100 000 in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal fractions, improper and mixed
skills.description: Show that different fractions can be the same amount, like 2/3 and 4/6. Switch between improper fractions and mixed numbers, like 7/4 and 1 and 3/4.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order fractions
skills.description: Tell which fraction is bigger, even when they are more than one whole. Use pictures, number lines, or the benchmark of one half to put fractions in order.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and compare hundredths
skills.description: Read, show, compare, and order decimals like 3.25. The second digit after the dot counts hundredths, and 3.2 is the same as 3.20.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round decimals to the tenth
skills.description: Round a number like 56.23 to the closest tenth, which is 56.2. If it is exactly halfway, like 56.25, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions, decimals, and percents
skills.description: Show that a fraction, a decimal, and a percent can name the same amount, like 1/4, 0.25, and 25%. Percent means out of 100.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Operation rules and checking answers
skills.description: Use rules like order, grouping, and splitting a number to make problems easier. Use opposite operations to check answers, even in problems with two steps.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide facts to 144
skills.description: Know all the times facts up to 12 × 12 and the divide facts that go with them. Know that zero times anything is zero.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times 0.1 and 0.01, estimate decimals
skills.description: In your head, multiply a whole number by 0.1 or 0.01, like 400 × 0.1 = 40. Round decimals to make a quick guess for adding and subtracting.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add, subtract big numbers and decimals
skills.description: Solve problems by adding and subtracting whole numbers up to 100 000 and decimals to hundredths. Line up the places, and trade when you need to.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract same-size fractions
skills.description: Add and subtract fractions that have the same bottom number, like 3/8 + 2/8. You are just adding or taking away pieces of the same size.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply two-digit by two-digit
skills.description: Multiply numbers like 24 × 38 using a rectangle split into four parts. Then do it with the written method.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide by a two-digit number
skills.description: Divide a three-digit number by a two-digit number, like 234 ÷ 18. Use a rectangle or the written method, and decide what to do with any leftover.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply and divide by unit fractions
skills.description: Find 4 × 1/3 by adding four one-thirds. Find 4 ÷ 1/3 by asking how many thirds fit in 4 wholes.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal ratios and rates
skills.description: Make ratios and rates that mean the same thing by scaling up or down, like 6 green to 1 yellow is 12 green to 2 yellow. Use tables and pictures to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 1 000 000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to one million in words, digits, and expanded form. Tell what each digit is worth, like the 5 in 527 910 is 500 000.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Positive and negative numbers
skills.description: Show numbers below zero, like -6, and numbers above zero, like 3, on a number line or with counters. Tell what -4 and 4 have in common.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build decimals to thousandths
skills.description: Read and show decimals like 7.635 in words, digits, and expanded form. Compare and order them by looking at the biggest place that is different.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare integers, decimals, and fractions
skills.description: Put negative numbers, decimals, and fractions in order, even when they are mixed together. Use a number line and benchmarks like 0, one half, and 1.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round decimals to tenth or hundredth
skills.description: Round decimals, even ones that go on forever like 3.555…, to the closest whole number, tenth, or hundredth. If it is exactly halfway, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions and decimals that match
skills.description: Change fractions into decimals and decimals into fractions, like 1/4 is 0.25 and 0.625 is 5/8. A fraction can also mean the top number divided by the bottom number.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Brackets and order of operations
skills.description: Use rules like order, grouping, and splitting numbers to make problems easier. Solve problems with more than one step, using brackets and the right order of operations.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divisibility rules
skills.description: Use quick tricks to tell if a number can be shared evenly by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, or 10. For example, add up the digits to check for 3 or 9.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Percents of numbers in your head
skills.description: Find percents like 1%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 25%, and 50% of a number in your head. For example, 10% of 350 is 35, so 5% is half of that.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract with decimals
skills.description: Solve stories by adding and subtracting whole numbers and decimals. Guess the answer first by rounding, then find the exact answer and check that it makes sense.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract different-size fractions
skills.description: Add and subtract fractions with different bottom numbers, like 1/2 + 3/4. Use fraction strips or a number line to make the pieces the same size.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Prime factors and factor trees
skills.description: Tell if a number is prime or composite. Break a number into prime factors with a factor tree, like 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply by tenths
skills.description: Multiply a three-digit number by a decimal like 0.3, as in 235 × 0.3 = 70.5. Use an area model or multiply by 3 and then take one tenth.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide by tenths
skills.description: Divide a number by a decimal like 0.5. Make both numbers 10 times bigger so you can divide whole numbers, like 5 ÷ 0.5 = 50 ÷ 5 = 10.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply a whole by a fraction
skills.description: Find 5 × 3/4 by thinking of 5 groups of three fourths. Use fraction strips or a number line, and give the answer as an improper fraction or mixed number.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide a whole by a fraction
skills.description: Find how many pieces like 3/4 fit into a whole number, such as 6 ÷ 3/4 = 8. Use pictures or rods to see the groups.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide decimals by whole numbers
skills.description: Divide decimals like 0.8 or 3.24 by a whole number up to 10, as in 0.24 ÷ 6 = 0.04. Use rods, grids, or short division.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Ratios, rates, and percents
skills.description: Solve problems with ratios, rates, and percents by scaling up or down. Use ratio tables to find equal ratios, like 2 cups of sugar for 4 cups of fruit.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Steps to Find Out Answers
skills.description: Put the steps for finding out about something in order. Pick a good question to look into and a good place to find the answer.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Fair Tests and Experiments
skills.description: Pick the test that changes only one thing. Put the steps of a simple experiment in order.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Design, Build, and Test
skills.description: Put the steps for making something in order: plan it, build it, test it, and make it better.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Staying Safe Like a Scientist
skills.description: Pick the safe way to use tools and materials. Choose the right gear to wear, like goggles or gloves.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Sharing What We Find Out
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you learned, like a chart, a picture, or a talk. Match the science words to what they mean.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Clear Coding Steps
skills.description: Look at a few lines of code and pick what they will do. Put the instructions in the right order so they are clear.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Coding and New Technology Today
skills.description: Pick how coding and new technology change things we do every day, like at home or in a store.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Science Helps Solve Problems
skills.description: Match science and technology tools at home and in town to the problems they fix. Pick how science can team up with subjects like math or art.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: People Who Help Science
skills.description: Match inventions and ideas to the different communities of people who gave them to us.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Everything in Nature Is Connected
skills.description: Sort living and non-living things in nature. Pick how they depend on each other, like a plant and soil.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: What Living Things Need
skills.description: Pick the things all living things need: air, water, food, heat, shelter, and space.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Body Parts That Help Survive
skills.description: Match a plant or animal part, like roots, fur, or wings, to the need it helps meet.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Parts of the Human Body
skills.description: Label the parts of the body, like eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin. Pick what each part does.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: A Healthy Place to Live
skills.description: Pick what makes a healthy environment, like clean air, clean water, and good food. Pick how it helps living things get what they need.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: How Living Things Help Each Other
skills.description: Match living things to how they help others, like bees helping flowers or trees giving shelter.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: What If Something Disappeared?
skills.description: Pick what could happen if a tree, a pond, or clean water went away. Think about how different people and animals would feel.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Ways to Help the Environment
skills.description: Pick actions that keep our air, water, and land healthy, like picking up litter.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Energy Moves and Changes Things
skills.description: Pick examples where energy makes something move or change, like a push, a wind, or heat melting ice.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: The Sun Gives Us Energy
skills.description: Pick how the Sun warms air, land, and water, gives us light, and helps plants grow.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Food Gives Energy
skills.description: Pick which things give living things energy. Match foods to animals and people that use them.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Where Our Energy Comes From
skills.description: Match everyday things, like lamps, cars, and stoves, to their energy source, like electricity, gas, wind, or sunlight.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Energy Resources Can Run Out
skills.description: Sort energy resources we get from the world around us. Pick which ones can run out.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Using Energy Wisely
skills.description: Pick ways we use energy at home and school. Choose ways to save it, like turning off lights.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Life Without Electricity
skills.description: Pick what would change for people and animals if there were no electricity.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Energy Through the Seasons
skills.description: Sort which energy we use in each season, like heaters in winter and fans in summer.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Objects and What They're Made Of
skills.description: Pick the materials, like wood, metal, plastic, or glass, that things are made from. Some objects use more than one material.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Structures That Hold Loads
skills.description: Pick which objects are built to hold weight. Find the frames that hold things up.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Describing Objects With Senses
skills.description: Pick words for how things look, feel, sound, and smell, like smooth, rough, or loud.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: What Objects Are For
skills.description: Match everyday objects and structures to what they are used for.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Right Material for the Job
skills.description: Pick the material property, like strong, soft, or waterproof, that helps an object do its job.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Fasteners and Their Uses
skills.description: Name fasteners like tape, glue, nails, screws, zippers, and buttons. Match each one to a job.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Where Materials Come From
skills.description: Match materials like wood, cotton, wool, and clay to the plant, animal, or earth they come from.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Waste and How to Make Less
skills.description: Sort kinds of waste, like paper, food, and plastic. Pick actions that make less waste and why they help.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Comparing Objects and Their Impact
skills.description: Compare objects with the same job, like a paper bag and a plastic bag. Pick what they are made of, where it comes from, and what happens when they wear out.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Earth and the Sun
skills.description: Pick how Earth turns and moves around the Sun to make day and night and the seasons.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Cycles That Repeat

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Maps of Land Use Effects
skills.description: Use maps and atlases to find boundaries, land uses, and resources in a region. Pick what a map shows about the land.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Graphs and Organizers About Land Use
skills.description: Read a line graph, bar graph, or organizer about forest cover or a mine. Pick the trend or effect it shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Conclusions About Land Use and Nature
skills.description: Look at the evidence about short and long term effects of land use. Pick the conclusion it supports and the best way to reduce harm.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sharing Land Use Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you learned, and the right words like stewardship, pollution, population, and natural resources.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Where Early Societies Lived
skills.description: Find early societies, like a First Nation and an Inuit society, on a globe or map. Read climate and land maps to see how the land shaped life.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Clues From Art and Artefacts
skills.description: Carvings, masks, beadwork, tools, and pottery are clues to how people lived long ago. Pick what each object tells about daily life.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Daily Life in Early Societies
skills.description: Match food, homes, clothing, school, and ceremonies to the early society they belong to, including First Nation and Inuit ones.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Land, Weather, and Early Food
skills.description: Rivers, floods, volcanoes, soil, and seasons changed how early people grew or found food. Match each feature or event to what it did.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Meeting Needs From the Land
skills.description: Early people got food, shelter, and clothing from where they lived. Match each place to how people met their needs.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Early Inventions and Discoveries
skills.description: Calendars, the printing press, farming tools, and boats were big ideas long ago. Match each invention to the people who made it and what it did.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Early Societies Were Governed
skills.description: Some societies had kings, emperors, chiefs, or voting councils. Match each way of governing to its society.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Classes and Groups Long Ago
skills.description: Societies had groups like nobles, peasants, slaves, priests, and merchants. Match each group to its role and how much power it had.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Why Groups Cooperated or Fought
skills.description: Groups worked together or fought over trade, land, power, and beliefs. Sort each reason into cooperation or conflict.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Making Peace Long Ago
skills.description: The Great Law of Peace, treaties, guilds, and sharing food helped people get along. Match each to how it helped.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Comparing Early Societies' Structure
skills.description: Compare how two early societies were organized, like classes and the status of women. Sort what is the same and different, and compare with Canada today.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Lives of Different Groups
skills.description: A slave and a senator, or a serf and a lord, lived very differently. Pick how their lives were different because of how their society was organized.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Young People Then and Now
skills.description: Children long ago had different chores, schooling, and play depending on their family. Sort what is like your life and what is different.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Caring for the Land Over Time
skills.description: Compare how early societies used land, seasons, and animals with how Canada does today. Sort what is the same and different.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Questions About Early Societies
skills.description: Pick a good question to investigate about how the land and weather shaped life in an early society.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sources About Early Societies
skills.description: Elders' stories, artefacts, images, and websites are sources. Sort which ones help answer a question about an early society.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Maps of Early Societies
skills.description: Read thematic maps of rivers, soil, climate, and trade routes. Pick what a map shows about where early people lived.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Organizers and Artefact Clues
skills.description: Use a Venn diagram, T-chart, or organizer to compare societies or study an artefact. Pick what the tool shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Conclusions About Early Societies
skills.description: Look at the evidence about how an early society and its land were connected. Pick the conclusion the evidence supports.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sharing Early Society Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you learned and the right words like serf, noble, Elder, hierarchy, and civilization.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Canada's Physical Regions
skills.description: Canada has mountains, plains, forests, and tundra. Match each region to where it is and what it is like.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: What People Do in Each Region
skills.description: Match activities like farming, mining, fishing, skiing, and hiking to the region where they happen.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Four Economic Sectors
skills.description: Sort industries like logging, car making, banks, and research into the resource, making, service, and information sectors.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Types of Political Regions
skills.description: Provinces, territories, towns, and First Nations are different kinds of regions. Match each to how it is the same or different.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Directions and Map Grids
skills.description: Use NE, NW, SE, SW and number-letter grids to find regions of Canada on a map.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Provinces, Territories, and Capitals
skills.description: Match each province and territory to its capital, where it is, and some of the people who live there.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Opportunities and Challenges in Regions
skills.description: Jobs, pollution, and housing can be good or hard for people in different parts of Canada. Sort each one into an opportunity or a challenge.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Nature Shapes Industry
skills.description: The Shield has mines, the Prairies have big farms, and the Maritimes have fishing. Match each region to the industry its land allows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Industries Affect Nature
skills.description: Oil sands, dams, smelters, and fishing can harm land, air, and water. Match each industry to its effect on the environment.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Using Resources More Sustainably
skills.description: Solar panels, safe fishing rules, and talking with Indigenous communities can help. Pick which actions work well and why.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Questions About Needs and Nature
skills.description: Pick a good question to investigate about balancing what people want with taking care of the environment.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Gathering Region Information
skills.description: Satellite images, thematic maps, climate graphs, and Elder interviews are sources. Sort which ones help with a Canadian region question.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Reading and Making Canada Maps
skills.description: Read population and resource maps and pick symbols or shading to make a map of Canadian resources or land height.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Graphs and Charts About Regions
skills.description: Read a double bar graph, population graph, or decision chart. Pick what it shows about people and the environment.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Conclusions About Needs and Nature
skills.description: Look at the evidence about an issue, like a new dam. Pick the conclusion it supports.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sharing Stewardship Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you learned and the right words like tundra, forestry, tourism, and hydroelectricity.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Indigenous Nations Before 1713
skills.description: Many Indigenous nations met Europeans long ago, like the Wendat, Mi'kmaq, Cree, and Inuit. Match each nation to where it lived and how it lived.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Nations Trading and Allying
skills.description: Before Europeans came, First Nations and Inuit traded, made alliances, and sometimes competed for waterways. Pick which one each story shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Why Europeans Came
skills.description: Explorers and settlers came for fur, fish, land, and to spread their religion. Match people like Cabot, Cartier, and Champlain to why they came.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Who Mattered in New France
skills.description: New France had a king, governor, bishop, intendant, seigneurs, and priests and nuns. Match each one to what it did for settlers.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Indigenous and European Meetings
skills.description: When Indigenous peoples and Europeans met, they traded, shared skills, fought, and spread disease. Match each event to what happened.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How the Métis People Began
skills.description: The Métis nation began when fur traders and First Nations women married and built families. Pick the reasons it began in the Great Lakes and Mattawa areas.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Ways of Life Differed
skills.description: Indigenous and European communities had different ways of governing, using land, and living. Match each difference to its reason, like climate or old customs.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: European Fights Reach Canada
skills.description: Wars between France and Britain pulled in First Nations and changed who controlled places like Acadia. Match each conflict to its effect.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Good and Bad Results of Contact
skills.description: Contact brought alliances and new ideas, but also disease, lost land, and conflict. Sort each result into positive or negative.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Who Gained From Whom
skills.description: Europeans gained from Indigenous knowledge of land, medicines, and routes. First Nations gained new tools. Match each group to what it gained.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Past Contact and Canada Today
skills.description: Old treaties and land use still link to land claims and treaty rights today. Match each past event to the issue it connects to now.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Questions About Early Contact
skills.description: Pick a good question about how a group, like coureurs de bois or First Nations women, saw early contact.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sources With Different Views
skills.description: Treaties, journals, petroglyphs, and oral histories are sources. Sort which ones give which group's view.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Maps of Contact and Trade
skills.description: Read maps of trade routes, First Nations territory, and Métis communities. Pick what each map shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Checking Evidence and Comparing Views
skills.description: Pick whether evidence is accurate and has an authentic voice. Use a comparison chart to compare views on the fur trade.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Conclusions About Early Contact
skills.description: Look at the evidence and pick the conclusion it supports about how different groups saw contact.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sharing Early Contact Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you learned, and words like treaty, missionary, settler, and wampum belt.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Rights and Responsibilities in Canada
skills.description: Citizens have rights like voting and free speech, and duties like respecting others. Sort each into a right or a responsibility.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Levels of Government and Services
skills.description: Federal, provincial, municipal, band councils, and school boards each run different services. Match each service, like police or garbage pickup, to who provides it.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: First Nations, Métis, Inuit Governments
skills.description: Groups like the Métis Nation of Ontario and the Haudenosaunee Confederacy govern today. Match each to who it represents.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Governments Sharing the Work
skills.description: Some jobs, like health care and the environment, are shared by several levels of government. Match each to the levels that share it.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Governments Ask the Public
skills.description: Elections, town halls, and referendums let people share their views. Match each way to how it works, and pick why asking people matters.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: The Duty to Consult
skills.description: Governments must talk with and make room for Indigenous communities about things like pipelines or mines on their land. Pick when this duty applies.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: What Governments Do About Issues
skills.description: Governments make recycling programs, laws, and language projects to solve problems. Match each action to the issue it helps with.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Why Views on Issues Differ
skills.description: Farmers, companies, governments, and Indigenous groups may see an issue differently. Match each group to why it feels that way.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Citizens Take Action
skills.description: People can sign petitions, vote, volunteer, or write to leaders. Pick the best action for each problem.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Did the Government Action Work?
skills.description: Look at what a government did about an issue and pick whether it worked well and why.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Plan for a Social Issue
skills.description: Put the steps of a plan about an issue like homelessness in order, and pick what governments and citizens should each do.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Plan for an Environmental Issue
skills.description: Put the steps of a plan about an issue like waste or clean water in order, and pick what governments and citizens should each do.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Questions About Canadian Issues
skills.description: Pick a good question to investigate an issue, like climate change in the Arctic, from the view of a government or Indigenous group.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Gathering Facts on Issues
skills.description: Sort sources, like Elder interviews, graphs, and government statements, by the view they show about an issue.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Maps of Issues
skills.description: Read maps that show things like areas hit by climate change or poverty across provinces. Pick what each map shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Graphs and Idea Webs on Issues
skills.description: Read line graphs, double bar graphs, and idea webs about an issue like recycling. Pick what they show.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Conclusions About Issues
skills.description: Use the evidence to pick a conclusion about an issue, and pick the strengths and weaknesses of different views.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sharing Issue Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you learned, and words like municipal, federal, MP, band council, and stakeholder.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Our Treaty and Traditional Territory
skills.description: Your community sits on traditional Indigenous land and inside a treaty area. Pick the territory and treaty names for your community.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Why People Came to Canada
skills.description: People moved to Canada for freedom, land, work, family, or to escape famine and war. Some were forced to come. Match each person's story to the reason.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Life in Newcomer Communities
skills.description: Newcomers farmed, worked, worshipped, and dressed in ways from their old homes. Match each way of life to its source, and pick how it affected Indigenous communities.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Kinds of Communities in Canada
skills.description: Canada has First Nations, French, British, later immigrant, religious, resource-town, and city communities. Match each kind to how it helped build the country.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Big Events for Indigenous Communities
skills.description: Treaties, the Indian Act, residential schools, and the creation of Nunavut changed First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities. Match each event to how it changed them.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Big Events for Newcomer Communities
skills.description: The Acadian expulsion, the Underground Railroad, and Japanese Canadian relocation shaped communities. Match each event to the community and how it changed them.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Jewish Communities in Canada
skills.description: Put key events in Jewish Canadian history in order, like the first synagogue and equal rights. Match unfair limits and how communities responded, like building Mount Sinai Hospital.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Communities Dealt With Each Other
skills.description: Communities traded, made treaties, helped each other, or treated each other unfairly. Sort each story into cooperation or conflict.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Communities Differed
skills.description: Communities differed in gender roles, money, religion, and beliefs about land. Match each difference to the communities it describes.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Change in My Own Community
skills.description: Your own community has changed over time. Pick the changes that fit a local, ethnic, or religious community and put them in order.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: What Makes Canada's Identity
skills.description: Canada values inclusiveness, human rights, diversity, bilingualism, parliamentary democracy, and treaties. Match each idea to what it means.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Features That Shape Canada's Image
skills.description: Memorials, mountains, winter, moose, mining towns, and city neighbourhoods all shape how people see Canada. Sort each into built, physical, or social, and pick what it adds to Canada's image.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Indigenous Gifts to Canada
skills.description: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit people gave Canada art, canoes, kayaks, medicines, Arctic knowledge, and democratic ideas. Match each gift to who made it.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Newcomer Gifts to Canada
skills.description: Chinese railway workers, Irish and Italian canal workers, the British parliament system, and French and English communities all helped shape Canada. Match each group to its gift.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Working Toward an Inclusive Canada
skills.description: Women's, labour, Indigenous, and disability groups worked for fairness. Match each group or law, like the Charter, to how it helped, and pick what still needs work.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Questions About Different Views
skills.description: One event can look different to different groups, like treaties or relocation. Pick a good question to investigate how each group saw it.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sources With Different Perspectives
skills.description: Letters, diaries, oral stories, treaties, and interviews are primary or secondary sources. Sort them, and sort which view each one shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Maps of Communities and Moves
skills.description: Read flow maps of relocations and thematic maps of where communities live. Pick what each map shows and how to build one.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Charts and Graphs on Perspectives
skills.description: Use a comparison chart, a census line graph, or photos and diaries to see how people felt. Pick what the tool shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Conclusions About Perspectives
skills.description: Check if evidence is strong and fair. Pick the conclusion about how different communities felt that the evidence supports.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sharing Perspective Findings
skills.description: Pick the best format to share different views, and the right words like immigrant, settler, colonization, and racism.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Canada Deals With Other Countries
skills.description: Canada works with other nations through trade deals, alliances, environmental agreements, and aid. Match each way to an example.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Canada in International Groups
skills.description: Canada takes part in the UN, WHO, NATO, NAFTA, UNICEF, and the Blue Flag Program. Match each one to what it does.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Groups Helping the World
skills.description: NGOs like Doctors Without Borders, companies, and groups like the UN and the Commonwealth work on world issues. Sort each group by its type and match it to its work.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Helping After Disasters
skills.description: Canada and NGOs helped after the Haiti earthquake, the Indian Ocean tsunami, and health crises. Match each disaster to the help given.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Canada, the Holocaust, and Human Rights
skills.description: Canada turned away Jewish refugees, like the MS St. Louis. Later it helped write human rights laws like the Charter. Match each action to what it did.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: How Canada Affects Other Regions
skills.description: Peacekeeping, trade deals, and education projects change life in other places. Match each action by Canada to its effect.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Finding Places Using Latitude and Longitude
skills.description: Find countries Canada works closely with on a map. Use latitude and longitude to find cities like London, Tokyo, and Nairobi.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Canada's Trading Partners
skills.description: The United States, Mexico, and China are big partners for Canada. Pick why, like being close, having stable governments, or needing products.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Trade and Jobs in Canada
skills.description: Trade deals, lower labour costs elsewhere, and immigration change jobs and money in Canada. Match each cause to its effect.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Canada's Global Links and Nature
skills.description: Shipping brings invasive species, cheap cotton and cocoa can harm farmland, and tree-planting helps. Match each link to its effect on nature.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Why Canada Joins Accords
skills.description: Canada joins groups to trade, stay safe, stay healthy, and protect rights. Match each group to why Canada joined and how much it matters.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Responses to a Global Issue
skills.description: Governments, NGOs, and people respond to issues like SARS, child labour, or refugees. Match each response to who did it.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Environmental Issues Everyone Shares
skills.description: Global warming, overfishing, and e-waste cross borders. Pick why many countries must work together to fix them.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Questions About Global Issues
skills.description: Pick a good question to investigate a world issue like fresh water, child labour, or climate change, its impact, and responses.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Gathering Facts on Global Issues
skills.description: Satellite images, online data, atlases, and eyewitness accounts are sources. Sort which ones help with a global issue question.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Maps of Global Issues
skills.description: Read maps of refugee areas, disease spread, and quality of life, or flow maps of imports. Pick what each map shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Graphs and Data on Global Issues
skills.description: Read climate graphs, bar graphs, and organizers about aid or drought. Pick what the data shows.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Conclusions About Global Issues
skills.description: Judge the evidence about a world issue and pick the conclusion it supports.

skills.subject: social-studies
skills.title: Sharing Global Issue Findings
skills.description: Pick the best format to share what you learned, and the right words like NGO, accord, aid, and relief efforts.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Why Our Bodies Need Food
skills.description: Food gives you energy and helps your teeth, skin, bones, muscles, and brain grow strong. Pick the reasons why we need food.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Staying Safe: Phones and Helpers
skills.description: Know your phone number, when and how to call 9-1-1, and which trusted adults can help you. Learn safe pickup routines too.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Body Parts and Correct Names
skills.description: Match the right names to parts of the body, using respectful, body-positive words.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: The Five Senses
skills.description: Name our five senses and match each one to the body part that does the job. Find out what each sense tells our brain.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Caring for Body and Mind
skills.description: Your mind is part of your health, just like your body. Pick things you can do to take care of both.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Using Canada's Food Guide
skills.description: Canada's Food Guide shows foods that help us eat well. Sort foods and pick healthy choices for a plate.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Hunger, Thirst, and Fullness
skills.description: Tell what your body feels when you are hungry, thirsty, or full. Pick what to do when you notice each one.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Caring and Harmful Behaviours
skills.description: Sort kind, caring things from hurtful ones, like bullying or unsafe touching. Pick how they feel and what to do, including asking for consent.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Being Safe at School
skills.description: Pick the safe things to do at school, like telling your teacher about allergies and playing in safe places. Choose safe ways to get to and from school.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Germs and Clean Habits
skills.description: Put hand washing steps in order and pick ways to stop germs from spreading. Think about tissues, sleeve sneezes, brushing teeth, and not sharing hats.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Spotting Dangers and Risks
skills.description: Find things that could hurt you at home, outside, near water, on the road, or online. Pick the safe choice.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Habits That Harm or Help
skills.description: Sort habits like too much screen time, smoking, and vaping from healthier choices. Pick ways to help someone choose healthier habits.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Thoughts, Feelings, and Actions
skills.description: What we think, feel, and do can change how our mind feels. Match thoughts and actions to good or poor mental health.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Staying Safe Everywhere
skills.description: Pick safe choices at home, outdoors, and online. Think about the phone and door, fire escapes, sun, buses, bikes, animals, and not sharing private information.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Food Allergies and Reactions
skills.description: Match common food allergies, like peanuts, milk, eggs, and fish, to the reactions they can cause. Pick the signs that a reaction is happening.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Medicines and Safe Use
skills.description: Sort medicines into ones a doctor prescribes and ones you can buy without a prescription. Pick the safe rules for using any medicine.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Stages of Human Life
skills.description: Put the stages of life in order, from infant to older adult. Pick what helps people grow and stay healthy at every stage.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Appreciating Your Changing Body
skills.description: Pick the amazing things your body can do. Choose ways to take care of and appreciate your body as it grows and changes.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Body and Brain Under Stress
skills.description: Match how your body and brain can feel in hard or uncomfortable times, like tired, hot, or overwhelmed. Pick what helps you feel better.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Food Guide Healthy Choices
skills.description: Use Canada's Food Guide to pick foods and drinks that help you eat well. Choose water and sort foods into healthy eating patterns.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Choosing Meals and Snacks
skills.description: Pick healthy meals and snacks. Sort what you can control, like choosing a snack, from what you can't, like allergies or what food is at home.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Consent and Standing Up
skills.description: Know why consent matters and pick ways to say no, state your boundaries, and respect others' no. Choose when to tell a trusted adult.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Taking Care of Your Teeth
skills.description: Pick the habits that keep your teeth and mouth healthy, like brushing, flossing, and visiting the dentist. Put tooth care steps in order.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Naming Your Feelings
skills.description: Match feeling words like calm, sad, angry, and worried to situations. Pick when a feeling means it's time to ask for help.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Getting Along With Others
skills.description: Pick kind ways to treat family and others, like cooperating, listening, and watching body language. Sort out hurtful behaviours like name calling, ignoring, and hitting.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Staying Healthy Without Medicine
skills.description: Match health problems to things that can help besides medicine, like sleep for a cold or fresh air for a headache. Pick healthy meals and traditional healing practices.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Where Food Comes From
skills.description: Find out where food is grown, fished, or hunted and how it is made ready. Pick how these things change how healthy food is and how they affect the Earth.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Concussions and Staying Safe
skills.description: Learn what a concussion is and how it can happen. Put the school's steps in order when someone bumps their head.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Substances and Dependency
skills.description: Sort substances like nicotine, caffeine, and alcohol. Pick how too much use can hurt your body, your mind, and other people.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Healthy Friendships and Consent
skills.description: Pick what makes a relationship healthy, like listening and being honest. Choose good ways to answer bullying and to ask for consent.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: What Helps Us Grow
skills.description: Pick things like sleep, food, and caring adults that help your body and feelings grow. Choose ways to feel good about your body.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Fight, Flight, Freeze
skills.description: Learn how your brain reacts when it thinks there is danger. Match fight, flight, and freeze to how you might think, feel, and act.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Food Choices and Healthy Teeth
skills.description: Learn why a healthy mouth matters for your whole body. Sort foods and drinks that help or hurt your teeth.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Safety Rules for Places
skills.description: Pick the best safety rules for places like water, camping, online, and fire plans. Choose safe ways to act around animals and with allergies.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Making Healthy Choices
skills.description: Think about what to consider when using medicine or screens. Pick the choice that keeps you from getting hooked or hurt.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Foods From Many Places
skills.description: Match foods like lentils, naan, berries, and fish to the cultures they come from. Pick how trying them adds healthy choices.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Pretend Violence vs Real Life
skills.description: Spot how shows and games make fighting look harmless. Pick what can really happen to people when violence is real.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Everyone Is Unique
skills.description: Sort differences you can see from ones you can't. Pick kind ways to show respect for others.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Big Feelings and What Causes Them
skills.description: Match things like moving, loud noise, or losing a pet to big feelings like worry. Pick ways to help yourself feel better.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Key Nutrients in Food
skills.description: Match nutrients like carbohydrates, protein, fat, vitamins, and minerals to foods that have them. Pick why your body, brain, and muscles need each one.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Risks and Safety Online
skills.description: Pick the risks of too much screen time, texting, gaming, and the Internet, like losing sleep or meeting online strangers. Choose smart ways to stay safe.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Bullying and Unsafe Behaviour
skills.description: Sort kinds of bullying, including cyberbullying, and other behaviour that is not okay. Pick how it can make someone feel and the best way to respond.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: What Is in Tobacco and Vapes
skills.description: Match substances like nicotine, tar, and carbon monoxide to tobacco and vaping products and smoke. Pick how each one can hurt your health.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Changes at Puberty
skills.description: Sort the body changes that happen at puberty, like growing taller and body odour. Pick feelings and social changes that can come with them.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Tracking Eating Habits and Goals
skills.description: Read a simple food log and pick a healthy eating goal that fits Canada's Food Guide, like choosing water or eating more vegetables.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Steps for Safe Decisions
skills.description: Put the steps of making a safe choice in order. Use them to pick the safest option when cycling, cooking, or going online.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Choosing Not to Smoke or Vape
skills.description: Pick strong ways to say no to smoking and vaping, like giving a reason or changing the topic. Sort what can push a choice, like peer pressure.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Hygiene as You Grow
skills.description: Pick the hygiene habits that matter more at puberty, like showering, clean clothes, and using hygiene products. Remember hand washing and tooth care too.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Daily Choices for Mind Health
skills.description: Pick everyday choices that help your mind, like sleep, being active, mindfulness, feeling check-ins, and helping others.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Healthy Eating Everywhere
skills.description: Pick ways to help people eat healthier at school, arenas, stores, camping, or a friend's house.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Effects of Smoke and Vaping
skills.description: Sort short- and long-term effects of smoking and vaping on smokers. Pick how second-hand smoke can hurt people nearby.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Managing Stress
skills.description: Pick strategies for stress you can control, and ways to cope with changes you can't, like moving or family stress.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Trusted People and Help Services
skills.description: Pick the trusted people and services, like Kids Help Phone, 9-1-1, and Telehealth, that can help with emergencies, bullying, and photo sharing without consent. Match each problem to who can help.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Alcohol: Effects and Intoxication
skills.description: Sort the short- and long-term effects of alcohol on the body and mind. Pick what changes how strongly alcohol affects a person, like amount, speed, body size, or mixing with other drugs.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Reproductive Parts and Puberty
skills.description: Label the parts of the reproductive system. Sort the body changes that happen during puberty.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Menstruation and Sperm Making
skills.description: Put the steps of the menstrual cycle and of sperm making in order. Pick how each one connects to making a baby and to growing up.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Reading Food Labels
skills.description: Read a nutrition fact table and an ingredient list. Pick the food that is the healthier and safer choice, for example for allergies, sugar, or sodium.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Handling Threatening Situations
skills.description: Pick the smart way to act when something feels unsafe: stay calm, notice your surroundings, say no firmly, and get help. Put the steps of a safety plan in order.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Saying No to Risky Pressure
skills.description: Pick strong ways to say no to pressure about alcohol, vaping, gambling, or too much gaming. Choose the best decision after thinking it through.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: What Shapes How You See Yourself
skills.description: Sort the things that shape how a person sees themselves, like strengths, culture, body image, friends, and stereotypes. Pick how these can help a person feel good about who they are.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Puberty Stress and Feeling Well
skills.description: Match the worries that can come with puberty, like crushes and changing friendships, to ways to cope. Pick signs that someone may need extra help and who to talk to.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Helping Friends With Mental Health
skills.description: Pick what you can do to support a friend who is struggling, like listening and being kind. Know when it is time to bring in a trusted adult.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Ads and Food Choices
skills.description: Spot how ads, packaging, celebrities, and social media try to change what we eat. Pick good questions to check if a claim or body image is true.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: How Our Actions Affect Others
skills.description: Sort hurtful actions, like name calling, exclusion, and sharing pictures online, from kind ones. Pick how each can change feelings, self-esteem, and reputation.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Why People Choose Alcohol or Cannabis
skills.description: Sort the things that can affect a choice to drink alcohol or use cannabis, like friends, media, laws, culture, and feelings. Pick how they can change at different ages.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Attitudes and Mental Health Stigma
skills.description: Pick attitudes and words that hurt people with mental health problems and ones that help. Choose how to stop stigma.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Being Inclusive and Respectful
skills.description: Being inclusive, respectful, and accepting helps everyone, including you. Pick actions that make others feel welcome.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Effects of Cannabis and Other Drugs
skills.description: Sort the effects of cannabis, opioids, and other drugs and things like glue or gas. Pick how they can hurt the body and mind.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Explicit Media and Real Life
skills.description: Pick how viewing sexually explicit media can give a wrong idea about relationships, gender, and bodies.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Finding Mental Health Support
skills.description: Match problems with mental health or substance use to people and services that can help. Pick how to reach them.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Thoughts, Emotions, and Actions
skills.description: See how thoughts, feelings, and actions connect. Sort positive and negative thinking and how each affects your mind.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: What Shapes Our Food Choices
skills.description: Sort things that affect what we eat, like allergies, cost, feelings, media, and culture. Pick healthy eating guidelines that fit.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Hunger Cues and Growing Bodies
skills.description: Match what changes how hungry you are, like growth spurts, activity, and big portions. Pick eating guidelines that listen to your body.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Handling Conflict Positively
skills.description: Pick ways to stay calm, listen, and speak up kindly in a conflict, in person or online.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Safe Choices About Drugs
skills.description: Sort what can push a choice about alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, or vaping. Use decision steps to pick a safe choice, including saying no.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Growing Up: Body, Friends, Feelings
skills.description: Sort the body, friend, and feeling changes of the teen years. Pick how knowing about them builds confidence.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Respect and Consent in Relationships
skills.description: Pick respectful choices that show you understand consent. Use skills like knowing yourself and managing feelings.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Healthy Eating and Active Living
skills.description: Match how eating well and being active together help your body and mind. Pick ways to encourage others to do both.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Safe When Caring for Others
skills.description: Pick safe choices when babysitting, staying home alone, or cooking. Choose what to do in emergencies like fire, allergic reactions, or bullying.

skills.subject: health
skills.title: Stereotypes and Fair Thinking
skills.description: Spot stereotypes about gender, race, culture, abilities, and more. Pick ways to answer them and how they affect people.
